# Pi.js 2.1.0 - Quick Reference for LLMs

## Overview

Pi.js is a browser-only WebGL 2 library for retro-style graphics, bitmap text, sound, and input.
The global API is available as `pi` and, when it is not already defined, `$`.

## Key Facts

- Current version: 2.1.0
- Create a screen before calling screen-scoped commands.
- Coordinates start at the top-left and use logical screen pixels.
- Rendering is automatic and pixel-perfect.
- Most commands accept positional arguments or one options object.
- Index 0 in a palette is reserved for transparent black.

## Setup and Drawing

```javascript
const main = $.screen( "320x200" );
$.setColor( "white" );
$.line( 0, 0, 100, 100 );
$.rect( 20, 20, 80, 40, "red" );
$.circle( 160, 100, 30, "blue" );
$.print( "Hello, Pi.js!" );
```

Aspect strings use `x` for exact dimensions, `m` for integer-multiple scaling, and `e` for
extending the logical area to fill the container:

```javascript
$.screen( "640x480" );
$.screen( "320m200", "game-container" );
$.screen( { "aspect": "320e200", "container": "game-container" } );
```

## Images and Resources

Load resources before waiting for readiness. `loadImage()` returns the registered image name;
`getImage()` retrieves its browser image element.

```javascript
const playerName = $.loadImage( "player.png", "player" );

$.ready( function() {
	$.screen( "320x200" );
	$.drawImage( playerName, 160, 100, null, 0.5, 0.5, 2, 2, 45 );
	const playerElement = $.getImage( playerName );
	console.log( playerElement.width, playerElement.height );
} );
```

`drawImage()` arguments after `x` and `y` are `color`, `anchorX`, `anchorY`, `scaleX`, `scaleY`,
and `angle` in degrees. Use `createImageFromScreen()` to capture framebuffer pixels.

```javascript
const captureName = $.createImageFromScreen( "capture", 0, 0, 63, 63 );
$.drawImage( captureName, 100, 20 );
$.removeImage( captureName );
```

Queued draws finish before `removeImage()` releases textures. Later draws using the removed name
throw `IMAGE_NOT_FOUND`.

## Colors and Settings

```javascript
$.setPal( [ "black", "white", "red", "green", "blue" ] );
$.setPalColors( [ 2, 3 ], [ "orange", "lime" ] );
const orangeIndex = $.getPalIndex( "orange", 0 );
const orange = $.getPalColor( orangeIndex );

$.set( {
	"color": orange,
	"blend": "alpha",
	"bgColor": "#101020"
} );
```

Supported blend modes are `"replace"` and `"alpha"`. Palette changes affect future drawing; they
do not recolor pixels already in the framebuffer.

## Views and Input

Views create nested local coordinate systems and clipping regions. Inside a view, `width()` and
`height()` return the requested view dimensions. Pointer coordinates remain screen-relative.

```javascript
$.screen( "320x200" );
$.pushView( 20, 20, 120, 80 );
$.cls();

const mouse = $.inmouse();
const localMouse = $.screenToView( mouse.x, mouse.y );
if( mouse.buttons & 1 ) {
	$.circle( localMouse.x, localMouse.y, 3, "white" );
}

$.popView();
$.resetView();
```

Keyboard polling and events start tracking automatically:

```javascript
if( $.inkey( "ArrowLeft" ) ) {
	playerX -= 1;
}

$.onkey( "Space", "down", function( keyData ) {
	console.log( keyData );
} );
```

Mouse and press callbacks receive one data object. Touch callbacks receive an array of touch
objects.

## Shaders

`applyShader()` inserts a pass into framebuffer draw order. A display shader changes final
presentation without modifying the logical framebuffer.

```javascript
const invert = $.createShader( `#version 300 es
precision mediump float;
in vec2 v_texCoord;
uniform sampler2D u_texture;
out vec4 fragColor;

void main() {
	vec4 color = texture( u_texture, v_texCoord );
	fragColor = vec4( 1.0 - color.rgb, color.a );
}` );

$.screen( "320x200" );
$.circle( 160, 100, 40, "red" );
$.applyShader( invert );
console.log( $.getShaderInfo( invert ) );
$.removeShader( invert );
```

Shader source must use GLSL ES 3.00 and declare `uniform sampler2D u_texture`. Known uniforms with
invalid values throw synchronously.

## Parented Offscreen Screens

```javascript
const main = $.screen( "320x200" );
const layer = $.screen( {
	"aspect": "160x100",
	"isOffscreen": true,
	"parent": main
} );

layer.circle( 80, 50, 30, "red" );
main.drawImage( layer, 80, 50 );

layer.removeScreen();
main.removeScreen();
```

The parent shares its WebGL context but does not own the child. Remove both screens explicitly.

## Ready and Game Loops

```javascript
await $.ready();
$.screen( "320x200" );

function gameLoop() {
	$.cls();
	updateGame();
	drawGame();
	requestAnimationFrame( gameLoop );
}

gameLoop();
```

## Migration Notes

Pi.js 2 removed the Canvas2D renderer, canvas-font and pen systems, manual `render()` control,
pixel-mode toggling, and unsupported blend modes. Pi.js 2.1 adds shaders, views, and parented
offscreen screens without removing documented 2.0 commands. Do not reproduce legacy calls from
older examples; consult `docs/UPGRADE-V2.txt` and `docs/UPGRADE-V2.1.txt` when migrating them.
